chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a mukatab who killed a man by mistake, and he said:

If his master, when making the contract with him, stipulated that if he became unable, he would return to slavery, then he is in the position of a slave: he is handed over to the heirs of the slain person, and if they wish they may enslave him, and if they wish they may sell him.

But if his master, when making the contract with him, did not stipulate that, and he had already paid something of his mukatabah, then ʿAli عليه السلام used to say: 'The mukatab is freed in proportion to what he has paid of his mukatabah, and it is upon the Imam to pay to the heirs of the slain person in proportion to what has been freed of the mukatab, and the blood of a Muslim man is not to be left uncompensated.'

And I hold that, for the portion that remains upon the mukatab of what he has not paid, he remains as a slave for the heirs of the slain person; they may make him serve them for his lifetime in proportion to what remains upon him, and they do not have the right to sell him.

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ ٱلْمَقْتُولِ: The legal heirs of the person who was killed.
key_terms.خَطَأً: By mistake; unintentionally, in the legal sense of accidental killing.
key_terms.رَدٌّ إِلَى ٱلرِّقِّ: Return to slavery if the conditions of the contract are not fulfilled.
key_terms.عَلَى ٱلْإِمَامِ أَنْ يُؤَدِّيَ: The Imam bears responsibility to pay the due amount in this case.
key_terms.لَا يُبْطَلُ دَمُ ٱمْرِئٍ مُسْلِمٍ: The blood of a Muslim is not to be rendered without legal recompense.
key_terms.مُكَاتَبٍ: A slave under a manumission contract to purchase his freedom gradually.
key_terms.يُعْتَقُ مِنَ ٱلْمُكَاتَبِ بِقَدْرِ مَا: He is freed in proportion to the amount he has already paid.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a mukatab accidentally kills a man in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a mukatab who kills someone unintentionally. It distinguishes between a contract that explicitly returns the mukatab to full slavery upon default and one that does not, and it assigns financial responsibility proportionate to the freedom already earned. It also emphasizes that the blood of a Muslim must not be left without due compensation.
